findings.printed: Theorem 7.12. Let F = k((t)) and let σ be an irreducible representation of G(F), with G unramified reductive over F. … Then σ is an irreducible constituent of an unramified principal series representation of G(F). / Lemma 10.7. If π satisfies case (b) of Lemma 10.6, then π is pure and ramified. / Proposition 10.10. Assume the residue field of F has more than 2 elements. Then every supercuspidal representation of GL(n,F) is ramified.

Let σ be a supercuspidal representation of G(F♯). Suppose the semisimple Fargues-Scholze parameter L^{ss}(σ) attached to σ is pure. Then L^{ss}(σ) is ramified. More generally, let σ be any pure irreducible representation of G(F♯) with unramified Fargues-Scholze parameter.
